_what: The hand-written half of the surface reconciliation. `bin/surface-oracle.swift` derives WHERE
the Mac app's surfaces live and WHAT THEY ARE CALLED, by being compiled against the shipped
`Destination.swift` and `RouterSheet.swift`. This file says WHICH CAMPAIGN SURFACE covers each
of those addresses. `bin/surface-reconcile.py` refuses when the two disagree in any direction.
The split is deliberate and is M35's, one file over in `scripts/acceptance/`. A fully derived
binding would have to invent a campaign surface for every address the app grows, which moves
the campaign's denominator with the app and stops it catching the thing it exists to catch: a
surface shipped with nobody having decided how to test it. Requiring a human to write the row
is the point. What is NOT left to a human is noticing that the row is missing.
A value is a LIST because one sheet kind can be presented by two boards. `confirm-remove` is
and `cleanup.resetHistory`. Binding either to a single surface would name one host and hide the
other. Coverage is satisfied when any bound surface carries a case, and every bound surface must
_boundLate: Three shipped addresses were listed HERE as deliberately unbound rather than in `bindings`,
and G18 left them so on purpose: writing the rows before a campaign surface existed would have
turned its own gate green over three addresses nobody had decided how to test. G15, G16 and G17
then enumerated the surfaces and wrote the cases — and none of them wrote the row. Measured
2026-08-27: `make surface-reconcile` stayed red at 5 disagreements with `covered: 19`, and this
file was byte-identical across `fabd028`, `ai/g16`, `ai/g17`, `ai/g18`, `ai/g19` and their
merge. Enumeration cannot clear SHIPPED-UNENUMERATED; only the binding can.
G25 writes the three rows. Each carries an expectation and not merely an address — that split
is the reason this file is hand-written at all:
destination:harnesses -> SURF-025. The Harnesses board on glass in three states, populated,
empty and failed-read, plus one headless row (CASE-0166) proving the rows are a live
router's. That row is not redundant with the glass ones: `ShellClientFactory` makes a Debug
build ALWAYS take a fixture, so no macos-glass capture can make that claim.
destination:insights -> SURF-026. The same three states, and one thing this board owes that
the others do not — a trace per drawn figure to something the router observes (CASE-0177).
DESIGN.md §6 forbids a number the router does not measure, and a plausible figure reads as
a real one, so a render alone would not discharge this address.
sheet:readme -> SURF-028. The capability-document panel the Servers board presents;
`RouterSheet.kind` maps `.servers(.document)` onto `.readme`, which is why the sheet axis
and not the destination axis carries it. Three tabs over one package, and the three
refusals distinguishable in the words the panel draws. Its frames come off an NSHostingView
backing store rather than the display (see that surface's shotNote), so this binding claims
the panel lays out and paints and does NOT claim MCPRouter.app was running.
SURF-025 and SURF-026 were BOUND, not recorded in `addressless`. Both have a product address
the app prints from its own enum, so an `addressless` row for either would be a written excuse
standing where the oracle already has a fact. SURF-028 never reached `addressless` at all: the
reverse check sweeps the `macos-glass` lane and that surface is on `swiftui`.

addressless.SURF-001: The shell itself — sidebar chrome, window title, menu bar. Not a destination and not a sheet; it is the frame the destinations are drawn in, so no address in `Destination` or `RouterSheet` names it.
addressless.SURF-009: The menu-bar popover and its inbox band. A separate scene from the console window, presented by the status item rather than by a board, so `RouterSheet` does not enumerate it.
